inline.s: You should know that Amitabha Buddha's grace and virtue toward us sentient beings are equal to the fruit-sea, inconceivable and immeasurable. All the grace and virtue in the world cannot compare with it. If we are in the Saha world amid the cycle of birth and death, then even if through the end of the future, life after life, we ground our bones to powder and shatter our bodies, it would be hard to recompense. Only if now, thought after thought with utmost sincerity, we enter the Buddha's real mark, and mind after mind without wandering dwell in the Buddha's right samadhi, and in all times hold the Buddha's name, making the thought of death imminent, awaiting the Buddha's coming to welcome us and our rebirth in the Land of Bliss — then above we perfect the Buddha-fruit and below we guide sentient beings, all returning together to the Land of Bliss, together verifying the Buddha-fruit. With this merit we recompense the Buddha's grace. If we can thus know grace and recompense grace, then when we recite the Buddha we naturally feel that the mind has somewhere to return and somewhere to rely upon. This too may be called 'now, thought after thought, seeing the Buddha [seeing the Dharmakaya of the Buddha], mind after mind drawing near the Buddha [drawing near the Dharmakaya of the Buddha].' Through this we can gradually turn the karmic consciousness, and not be turned by it. If it is thus now, it will also be thus at death. Hence the ancients said: the mind that is in samadhi at death is precisely the mind that is reborn in the Pure Land. Reborn thus, it is certain that a thousand will be reborn out of a thousand, a hundred out of a hundred. May all of us tread solid ground, be mindful thought after thought, and not neglect this.
The Pure Land Dharma-Gate, Ancient and Present, Same and Different

All we who practice the Buddha-recitation should investigate and verify whether the Pure Land Dharma-gate of the present time and that of ancient times are, in the end, the same or different. If we say they are different, then our Buddha-name, recited year after year from dawn to dusk, is still the six characters 'Namo Amitabha Buddha,' without the slightest difference from the Buddha-name of ancient times. If we say they are the same, then why is it that the ancients who went west were each particularly easy? If they did not go, then fine; but when they went, it shook heaven and moved the earth. Those of the highest grade, at death, were welcomed by the Buddha — heavenly music by the hundred and thousand, banners and canopies without number, white cranes soaring, and strange fragrance filling the room. Everyone could see it, everyone could hear it. When they wished to go, they went; and when they went, they needed no one to assist them. Dying seated or dying standing, they went off at their own will. Even down to ordinary practitioners, all could know the time of death in advance, bathe, change clothes, sit upright and recite the Buddha, see the Buddha come to welcome them [see the Buddha's physical body], and pass away peacefully. Reflecting on each of these, how admirable! Why is it that among people of the present time, seven out of ten have difficulty in being reborn? Even if they attain it, it is very strained and they must be assisted by others. Examining the auspicious signs at their death, many of the highest-grade rebirths of the present cannot match those of the middle and lower grades of ancient times; the middle and lower grades, needless to say. Looking through the records of the ancients' rebirths, free and liberated, there are not just a million — hard to enumerate. Let me now briefly cite a few, so that everyone may know and thereby believe it is true.

In the past there were two laymen who, in ordinary times, were friends in the Way, regarding each other as lotus companions for birth and death. They agreed that on the day of rebirth they would notify one another and the two would go together. Later, one of them left without announcing. The other, only the next day, heard his son say: 'My father yesterday, without illness, went west.' When the layman heard this, he at once said: 'This old fellow has gone without a word; I need only the effort of a moment to catch up with you.' Thereupon he bathed, changed clothes, sat upright, recited the Buddha, and passed away. There was also a venerable monk, even more extraordinary. When it was time to go, he said himself: 'I am returning to the West, and wish to take an attendant along; who is willing to go with me?' None answered. Beside him a child replied: 'I will go with the Master.' The monk said: 'Go and bid farewell to your mother.' Because his mother took it as a joke and thought nothing of it, she casually agreed. Unexpectedly the child returned to the temple, and at once sat upright, recited the Buddha, and passed away. The monk, patting his head, said: 'Little one, why have you gone ahead of me?' The monk also at once joined his palms, recited the Buddha, and departed. In the past, too, there was the layman Huaixi, who at death, without illness, announced: 'I am returning to the West.' His family said: 'Wait until we heat fragrant water for your bath.' He answered: 'I have long since bathed in fragrant water,' and, chatting and laughing, he departed. Observing these five people, at death they were wholly untroubled by karmic hindrances, liberated and free. There was also a monk reciting sutras who met a pheasant flying in from outside, wishing to peck at him. At once a spirit in golden armor appeared beside him, brandishing a staff and driving it away, saying: 'The great master is to be reborn in the West; how can you demand your life-debt from him?' From this one sees that those who truly obtain the benefit of the Buddha-recitation can have even the karma of fixed retribution averted — how much the more karma not fixed. Why is it that practitioners of the present time, at death, are mostly troubled by karmic hindrances, their minds unable to be in control, in extreme pain beyond description? We should investigate where the ancients' attainment lay, and where the present people's loss lies. If we do not investigate where their gain and loss lie, and make it manifest and clear, then those who do not understand will not be convinced, and will surely say: 'The Buddha has no response, the Dharma has no efficacy' — betraying the practitioners and making vain and useless toil, handed round from one to another, misleading people no little. In what follows I will clarify and distinguish, so that everyone may know: the ancients at death, without karmic bondage, liberated and free, were all because their ordinary-time practice was effective in power. Whether they practiced contemplation or held the name, they could all deeply enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark and dwell at ease in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi. Since they could deeply enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark and dwell at ease in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi, then all the ordinary defiling, karmic-consciousness realms naturally and gradually dissolved, turning to emptiness and stillness, even to annihilation, without the least remainder. There was only the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, all-pervading in the ten directions, filling the Dharma-realm. Therefore many of the ancients entered this real-mark right samadhi, refining the wondrous contemplation. Like holding a bright mirror, they saw their own image. Until the wondrous contemplation was accomplished, they personally verified the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark. The sublime realm of Ultimate Bliss, within right samadhi, appeared whenever they wished to see it. Whenever they recollected, it was immediately present. With a single thought present, they at once felt their body in the Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the past, the Fourth Patriarch, Master Fazhao, cultivating contemplation on Mount Lu, in samadhi personally reached the Land of Ultimate Bliss. He saw beside the Buddha a monk with a soiled robe covering his head. The Buddha said: 'This is Chengyuan of Mount Heng.' Therefore the master, upon arising from samadhi, personally went to Mount Heng to study under him, and at first sight became a faithful disciple. Not only those who cultivate contemplation — those who hold the name, if they have already deeply entered the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark and dwelt at ease in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi, and further are willing to practice with effort, cutting off delusion and verifying personally, the sublime realm of the Pure Land may also be seen in the present life. It is like a man entering the sea and seeing the dragon palace — what doubt is there? The ancients at death were able to be liberated and free, to go when they wished without needing assistance, all because they had personally verified the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark. Even if they had not personally verified it, they must have deeply attained the power of the Tathagata's real-mark right samadhi. All the above is what the ancients attained.

Why is that which the people of today have lost? Of the practitioners of the present time, they only know the provisional and not the real. Even if they practice, they can only apply effort on the provisional level; they cannot gather the provisional back into the real and be the provisional and the real non-dual, provisional and real one suchness. Hence the benefit they obtain is shallow and slight. The karma-power of countless kalpas is strong. For example, a cup of water — how can it extinguish a cartload of firewood? Again, like bathing: if the water is little and the dirt is heavy, how can one be clean? If one wishes to be clean, one must sit with the whole body in the bath, washing for a long time, and only then can it all be removed without remainder. We who practice the Buddha-recitation are likewise. If we wish the karma of the three times through countless kalpas to be pure and the three hindrances to be eliminated, then when we recite the Buddha we must with our whole body enter into Amitabha Buddha's samadhi sea, gradually perfumed and soaked, washed for a long time, and only then can our karmic hindrances be exhausted without remainder. That which the people of today have lost is lost in the powerlessness of their ordinary practice. Why? Because when they recite the Buddha ordinarily, the false does not return to the true; and at death, right samadhi can by no means appear. Because ordinarily their false thoughts flow, the still water of samadhi is dried up, appearances are jumbled and confused, and right wisdom is benighted. Though they have pure conduct, it is scattered; they cannot gather it and return it to a single mind. Even if there is merit, in the end it is provisional and small; hence at death the benefit is also small. It is like a fish in water, which relies entirely on the power of the water to move freely. If it obtains full water, it enjoys full bliss. If it obtains a great portion of water, it enjoys a great portion of bliss. If it obtains a little water, it feels only suffering and no bliss. If it obtains no water at all, in a moment it cannot move, and its life is gone. We who practice the Buddha-recitation are likewise. If one can personally verify the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, it is like obtaining full water. If one can deeply enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, it is like obtaining a great portion of water. If one only applies effort on the provisional level and cannot deeply enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark, it is like obtaining a little water. If one does not recite the Buddha at all, then one is wholly unconnected to the Tathagata's samadhi sea-water, and the life of wisdom is cut off.

From now on we who wish to enter the Tathagata's fruit-sea real mark and dwell at ease in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi — there are two kinds. What are the two? One is awakening; only the keen faculty can accomplish it. The second is utmost sincerity; both the keen and the dull can accomplish it. What is awakening? The so-called Amitabha Buddha's samadhi fruit-sea is originally real and full, filling the Dharma-realm. In every place, without exception, it is all-pervasive. All things in the ten directions are all contained within it. We, through countless kalpas, have always been within Amitabha Buddha's samadhi sea, vainly living and vainly dying, unaware and unknowing. Up to now, though the mouth recites the Buddha, the mind is in fact reluctant; still thought after thought flows, mind after mind wanders. We turn away from the Buddha and are separated from the Buddha. It is like an unfilial child, thought after thought keeping far from his parents, mind after mind going against his home village. We cannot dwell in the Buddha's samadhi right samadhi, nor accord with the Buddha's fruit-sea real mark. Now we should, thought after thought, turn about and reflect; mind after mind, awaken. How do we turn about and reflect? How do we awaken? Constantly contemplate that this present thought's five-aggregate body and mind of ours is originally within Amitabha Buddha's samadhi sea, neither going out nor coming in, dwelling at ease in right samadhi. And when a single thought does not flow, then a single thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi; when thought after thought does not flow, then thought after thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi. If it flows, gather it and cause it to return. Long-cultivated and matured, it needs no forcing. Naturally, thought after thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi, and mind after mind accords with the Buddha's real mark. From here on, reciting the Buddha, every phrase is powerful, every character flows from the Tathagata's real-mark right samadhi. It is said: the real mark is the great name, the great name is the real mark. If one can recite the Buddha thus, this is called thought after thought according with the Buddha, mind after mind uniting with the Buddha.

What is utmost sincerity? It is: while we are rightly reciting the Buddha, we can only, thought after thought, harbor utmost sincerity in the mind, put down the whole body, die to the mind and tread solid ground, without recourse to thought, honestly reciting on. Naturally, thought after thought turns away from the dust and unites with awareness, returns from the false to the true. Like a river entering the sea, gradually entering, gradually deepening. It is said: a single thought of utmost sincerity, then a single thought enters the Buddha's fruit-sea; thought after thought of utmost sincerity, then thought after thought enters the Buddha's fruit-sea. Since one can enter the Buddha's fruit-sea thought after thought, then while reciting the Buddha one constantly receives the Tathagata's six benefits. What are the six? One, constantly receiving the Tathagata's Dharmakaya nurture, enabling the practitioner to be at peace thought after thought. Two, constantly receiving the Tathagata's compassionate mind's protection, enabling the practitioner not to retreat thought after thought. Three, constantly receiving the Tathagata's samadhi power's upholding, enabling the practitioner not to be scattered thought after thought. Four, constantly receiving the Tathagata's real-mark fusion, enabling the practitioner to be full thought after thought. Five, constantly receiving the Tathagata's wisdom-light shining through, enabling the practitioner to be without hindrance thought after thought. Six, constantly receiving the Tathagata's wisdom power's penetrating clarity, enabling the practitioner to be thoroughly clear thought after thought. If one is of the keen faculty and receives these six benefits, in the present life one can produce all kinds of wisdom and all kinds of eloquence; in all speech the true and the worldly fuse, principle and fact are without obstruction. From here on, every phrase of the Buddha-name flows from the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-sea.' It is said: 'the whole is a single thought, a single thought is the whole.' You should know that to recite the Buddha thus is true Buddha-recitation. And to rely on the Buddha's power thus is relying on it to the utmost.

Even if in the present life one cannot cut off entirely the various afflictions and personally verify the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-sea, one still obtains the perfuming atmosphere of the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-sea. Hence the Great Being Mahasthamaprapta says: 'Like one who perfumes himself with incense, his body bears the fragrance — this is called the adornment of fragrance and light.' With this merit, direct it to the Land of Ultimate Bliss and make the vow to be reborn. Not only does one not lose the right cause of rebirth; upon being reborn, one's grade is high. Though one cannot, like the ancients, have any special auspicious sign that people can see and hear, one can, as death draws near, know the time in advance; the body is free from the suffering of illness, the mind is not benighted; right mindfulness is clear and distinct, and one is moved by the Buddha's guidance. At the time of death one is at ease, as if entering samadhi. From this one ends birth and death and transcends the ordinary to enter the holy — this is already quite sufficient.

If we wish to obtain the aforementioned genuine benefit, we should be mindful with utmost sincerity thought after thought and awaken mind after mind. Put down the whole body, single-mindedly recite the Buddha. Push forward with all our strength, not giving rise to falling back. Like coming out of a pit of excrement, like hastening toward a jewel-place. You should know that the lotus pool is before us and the cauldron of boiling broth is behind us. Once one enters the lotus pool, wondrous bliss is complete. Once one enters the cauldron of boiling broth, the pain is endless. If one can push forward with all one's strength, one is called a great man who has emerged from the world. One morning the Buddha comes to guide, and in a snap of the fingers one is reborn in the Land of Bliss. From here on, gradually advancing in cultivation, until above one perfects the Buddha-fruit and below guides sentient beings. One may say that the Buddha's grace and the patriarchs' grace are both recompensed, and that oneself and others are equally saved.
The Pure Land Dharma-Gate: Nature and Practice Non-Dual

The Pure Land Dharma-gate should take the nature-virtue as substance and the practice-virtue as function. Why? The Buddha said: all sentient beings possess Buddha-nature. And he said: all sentient beings have the Tathagata's wisdom-virtue and marks, but because of deluded thinking and clinging they cannot realize it. If one is free from deluded thinking, then all-wisdom, natural wisdom, and unobstructed wisdom immediately appear. Judging from this, one sees that the natural nature-virtue of sentient beings is originally wholly the same as the Buddha's. That which is different is only the karma-power of sentient beings. It is said: the Buddha, through countless kalpas, cultivated in accordance with his nature — called 'the nature-good cultivating good.' Until the good karma was cultivated to the utmost, merit and wisdom were full, and he dwells at ease in the Pure Land, forever enjoying wondrous bliss. Sentient beings, through countless kalpas, cultivate against their nature — called 'the nature-evil cultivating evil.' Until the evil karma is cultivated to the utmost, the hindrance of sin is deep and heavy, and they sink in the Avici hell, forever undergoing intense suffering. Judging from this, the two words 'nature' and 'practice' are of the greatest importance. But because of a single initial thought, a hair's breadth of error leads to the loss of an entire kalpa. Rising to bliss or sinking to suffering — heaven and earth are far apart. In truth, viewed with right vision, the single word 'nature' is originally thorough from top to bottom, most sudden and most complete. From the Buddhas of the ten directions above to the beings of the nine realms below, all equally possess the one nature, bright and complete, without duality or difference. But the gain and loss within it all rest on whether one uses the mind well or not. For example, a room in which a hundred thousand lamps are lit: although the lamps differ, in the end the light is one; the whole is the same, without the slightest difference. It is said: the lights contain one another, the lamps gather one another; they accord in full, becoming a light treasury. Like the great sun, illuminating without exception. But if among them there is one person holding a lamp, not using the mind well, carelessly dashing about and lighting fires everywhere, seeking only pleasure and not minding the danger — that person will surely bring calamity, and the danger is unpredictable. At the least he damages his property; at worst he loses his life. From this one can deeply understand that the two words 'nature' and 'practice' are of great importance; it goes without saying. Therefore the Buddhas cultivate in accordance with their nature; when their bright practice is complete, they become wisdom-virtue and marks. Sentient beings cultivate against their nature; bound by greed and defilement, they become deluded thinking and clinging. You should know that Amitabha Buddha, in the past countless kalpas, from first arousing the resolve on to Buddhahood, was at each step in accordance with nature. It is said: arousing the bodhi-mind — it was in accordance with nature that he aroused it. Establishing the great vows — it was in accordance with nature that he established them. Practicing through the kalpas — it was in accordance with nature that he practiced. Adorning with the ten thousand virtues — it was in accordance with nature that he adorned. Perfecting the fruit-awareness — it was in accordance with nature that he perfected it. Saving all beings — it was in accordance with nature that he saved them. From beginning to end, even to the end of the future, there is not the slightest thing beyond his nature.

Yet since the Tathagata's causal ground was thus in the past, our causal ground today should also be thus. Though sage and ordinary occupy different stations, and beings and Buddhas travel different paths, how does the nature-virtue of sentient beings in the end differ from the Buddha's? If viewed with the Buddha's eye, from the Buddhas of the ten directions above to the beings of the nine realms below, none are not within the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-awareness nature, all alike entering samadhi. Why? Because space is not great; the nature-virtue is greatest. Judging from this, one can know that we, through countless kalpas up to now, have always been within Amitabha Buddha's samadhi fruit-awareness nature, and have never departed from it. In all our times, when we stir the mind and think, doing good or doing evil, all is within the Tathagata's samadhi fruit-awareness nature, and the Buddha knows and sees it all. But because from beginningless time we have always been deluded, unaware and unknowing, we do not see the Tathagata's fruit-awareness true nature and do not know the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi. It is like a fish dwelling in water without knowing water, a bird flying in the sky without seeing the sky. Therefore Shakyamuni Tathagata, with a thoroughly compassionate heart, pitying us heavily-obstructed ordinary beings of the last age, who have no Buddha to be near: though there are the three-vehicle canons, we cannot practice them according to the Dharma. Even if we could practice them according to the Dharma, among ten thousand there is scarcely one who verifies personally. Even if one could verify personally, if one has not cut off delusion and karma completely, one still cannot transcend the three realms. Even if one cuts off delusion and karma completely and transcends the three realms, one has not fully verified the three non-retreat stages. If one wishes to reach bodhi directly, never falling back, this is not attainable. The World-Honored One, desiring to give free course to this compassionate intention, therefore of his own accord spoke the Amitabha Sutra. First he taught the arising of faith and the making of vows; next he taught the holding of the Buddha-name. For this Buddha-name was accomplished by the power of Amitabha Buddha's vows in former lives — the whole of his perfectly realized fruit-awareness is manifested in a single phrase of the great name. He universally causes us who recite the Buddha, as long as we harbor utmost sincerity thought after thought and call upon the Buddha's name, naturally to enter thought after thought into the Tathagata's perfect fruit-awareness and abide in the Tathagata's samadhi right samadhi. It is said: a single thought of utmost sincerity, then a single thought enters the Buddha's fruit-awareness; thought after thought of utmost sincerity, then thought after thought enters the Buddha's fruit-awareness. And a single thought not flowing, then a single thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi; thought after thought not flowing, then thought after thought dwells in the Buddha's right samadhi. Like a river entering the sea, gradually entering, gradually deepening. If there are deluded thoughts flowing, at once gather them and cause them to return. Long-cultivated and matured, it needs no forcing; naturally thought after thought accords with the Buddha's perfect fruit-awareness, mind after mind unites with it. Every phrase of the Buddha-name flows from the Tathagata's fruit-awareness right samadhi. Having entered the Tathagata's perfect fruit-awareness, from now on every practice is cultivating in dependence on nature, with all practice in nature.

It is said: if we arise faith thus, it is in accordance with nature that we believe. If we make vows thus, it is in accordance with nature that we vow. If we practice single-mindedly thus, it is in accordance with nature that we practice. If at death we are reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, it is in accordance with nature that we are reborn. When the flower opens and we see the Buddha in the West, it is in accordance with nature that we see. Hearing the Buddha teach and awakening to non-arising, it is in accordance with nature that we awaken. Until the Buddha-fruit is perfectly fulfilled, it is in accordance with nature that we are perfect. Saving sentient beings — it is in accordance with nature that we save them. From today onward, even to the end of the future, we are not the slightest bit beyond nature. Hence the ancients said: the present single mind is intrinsically endowed with the myriad dharmas and with wisdom-light; above, it equals the Buddha-mind; below, it is the same as all the sentient. You should know that Shakyamuni Tathagata teaches us who recite the Buddha that 'in seven days one attains single-mindedness,' which is the real and wondrous mind of Amitabha Buddha's perfect fruit-awareness. Entering this perfect fruit-awareness real and wondrous mind, fused for a long time, one naturally is not scattered. Furthermore, one comes to realize that within it there is no dharma not endowed, no dharma not fused. It is said: adorned with the ten thousand virtues, benefiting without end, intrinsically present. Pure and clear, with nothing attained, intrinsically empty. Empty and non-empty without obstruction, real and full, intrinsically the middle. The mind that can recite is the single mind of the three contemplations. The Buddha that is recited is the single realm of the three truths. If one takes the Buddha as the sole school, then the whole mind is immediately the Buddha. If one takes the mind as the sole school, then the whole Buddha is immediately the mind. If one takes the non-dual perfect fusion as the school, then mind and Buddha at once fuse. If one takes transcending emotion and seeing as the school, then mind and Buddha at once vanish. The substance of the nature-virtue alone is manifest, fully revealed. The whole is a single thought; a single thought is the whole. Substance and function are not two; substance and function are one suchness. This is precisely what is called 'adorned with the Buddha's adornment, self-adorned; upheld by the Buddha's upholding, self-upheld.'

If one can comprehend as above and cultivate by perfume-drenching without retreating, and with this merit direct it to the Land of Ultimate Bliss and make the vow to be reborn, then at the time of death Amitabha Buddha and the holy assembly, within this perfect fruit-awareness real and wondrous mind, will naturally appear and personally descend to guide us, and we will be reborn in the Land of Bliss. When the flower opens and we see the Buddha, our grade is certainly high. Why? Because to be reborn thus is to be born in non-birth, and birth without birth. Though all day one is earnestly seeking rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, one constantly accords with the principle of non-arising. The above is what is meant by 'the Pure Land Dharma-gate, nature and practice non-dual' — a profound and wondrous, inconceivable principle. All those of every religion who do not believe in reciting the Buddha and seeking rebirth in the West have not deeply entered Amitabha Buddha's perfect fruit-awareness. If one has deeply entered Amitabha Buddha's perfect fruit-awareness, and knows that from today onward, even to the end of the future, benefiting oneself and others, profound and wondrous without end, until bodhi without ever falling back — then if someone wished to obstruct him, not allowing him to recite the Buddha and seek rebirth in the West, surely ten thousand oxen could not pull him back. May all who understand deeply ponder it.
The Pure Land Dharma-Gate Has Fact and Principle

The fact of the Pure Land Dharma-gate is the fact that is principle; apart from principle there is no fact. The principle of the Pure Land Dharma-gate is the principle that is fact; apart from fact there is no principle. If one comprehends its principle, then at once the One True alone is manifest, profound and wondrous beyond thought; even great wisdom rarely reaches its limit. If one investigates its fact, then at once the ten thousand virtues all appear, shallow and near, easy to attain; even the foolish and ordinary can enter its gate. But the fact of the Pure Land Dharma-gate is supremely special, different from all other gates. The principle of the Pure Land Dharma-gate is entirely the same as all other gates. Why? What is supremely special: from Amitabha Buddha's first establishing the vows and his practice in the causal ground, he is transcendent and utterly different from the Buddhas of the ten directions. Therefore his fruit-ground enjoyment, the magnificence and purity of his land, and his skill in saving beings are also supremely special, different from all other gates. And what is entirely the same: from Amitabha Buddha's final attainment of Buddhahood, with merit and wisdom both full, his realized fruit-awareness fuses the three truths, truth exhausted and delusion exhausted; he perfectly breaks through ignorance and perfectly verifies the Dharmakaya; filling and pure, encompassing the Dharma-realm, he is called the Dharma-realm Body of the Treasury, equal and without difference to what all the Buddhas of the ten directions have realized. Therefore the Pure Land Dharma-gate — all fact is principle, all principle is fact, fact and principle fuse, fact and principle are one suchness — is also entirely the same as all other gates. All the merit and wondrous practice, the fact and principle cultivation, of the Pure Land Dharma-gate flow from this Dharma-realm. It is said: every dharma flows from this Dharma-realm, and every dharma returns to this Dharma-realm. Now, in what follows, I will briefly set forth the meaning of the fact-and-principle, same-and-different, of the Pure Land Dharma-gate, so that all of you may know.
